explanation: The king of Assyria who attacked Judah and besieged Jerusalem during the reign of King Hezekiah.
The king of Judah who sought God's help when Jerusalem was threatened by Sennacherib and his army.
A high officer in the Assyrian army, sent by Sennacherib to persuade the people of Jerusalem to surrender.
The capital city of the kingdom of Judah, the center of Jewish faith and worship of God.
An ancient kingdom in southern Israel, ruled by King Hezekiah at the time of Isaiah chapter 36.
A divine messenger from God who carries out God's will and protects His people.
Also known as the temple in Jerusalem, the place where the Jews worshiped God and performed religious rituals.
To set free or rescue someone from a dangerous or difficult situation. In this context, it refers to God's act of saving Jerusalem from the Assyrians.
